claim: Purified microtubules align along the static magnetic field (SMF) in vitro because of their diamagnetic anisotropy.
source: Purified microtubules have been shown to align along the static magnetic field (SMF) in vitro because of their diamagnetic anisotropy.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that references established knowledge about microtubule behavior in magnetic fields.

claim: The biological effects of SMF of above 20 T on mammalian cells have never been reported prior to this study.
source: In particular, the biological effects of SMF of above 20 T (Tesla) on mammalian cells have never been reported.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract as background context for the novelty of the study.

claim: In both CNE-2Z and RPE1 human cells, spindle orients in 27 T SMF.
source: Here we found that in both CNE-2Z and RPE1 human cells spindle orients in 27 T SMF.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3-7.

claim: The direction of spindle alignment depends on the extent to which chromosomes are aligned to form a planar metaphase plate.
source: The direction of spindle alignment depended on the extent to which chromosomes were aligned to form a planar metaphase plate.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 5-6.

claim: The magnetic torque acts on both microtubules and chromosomes.
source: Our results show that the magnetic torque acts on both microtubules and chromosomes, and the preferred direction of spindle alignment relative to the field depends more on chromosome alignment than microtubules.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on experimental observations.

claim: The preferred direction of spindle alignment relative to the field depends more on chromosome alignment than microtubules.
source: Our results show that the magnetic torque acts on both microtubules and chromosomes, and the preferred direction of spindle alignment relative to the field depends more on chromosome alignment than microtubules.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by experiments with CENP-E inhibitor shown in Figure 6.

claim: Spindle morphology was perturbed by 27 T SMF.
source: In addition, spindle morphology was also perturbed by 27 T SMF.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: This is the first reported study that investigated the mammalian cellular responses to ultra-high magnetic field of above 20 T.
source: This is the first reported study that investigated the mammalian cellular responses to ultra-high magnetic field of above 20 T.
evidence: This claim is explicitly stated in both the abstract and discussion sections.

claim: Spindle orientation is central to cell fate determination and tissue architecture.
source: Spindle orientation is central to cell fate determination and tissue architecture, and mounting evidences show that astral microtubules, multiple cortical proteins and their interactions with plasma membrane are all critical to achieve correct orientation (Toyoshima et al., 2007; Lancaster and Knoblich, 2012; Lu and Johnston, 2013; Bergstralh and St Johnston, 2014; Nestor-Bergmann et al., 2014).
evidence: This is background knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Astral microtubules, multiple cortical proteins and their interactions with plasma membrane are all critical to achieve correct spindle orientation.
source: Spindle orientation is central to cell fate determination and tissue architecture, and mounting evidences show that astral microtubules, multiple cortical proteins and their interactions with plasma membrane are all critical to achieve correct orientation (Toyoshima et al., 2007; Lancaster and Knoblich, 2012; Lu and Johnston, 2013; Bergstralh and St Johnston, 2014; Nestor-Bergmann et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Most biological materials are diamagnetic, such as proteins, DNA and lipids.
source: Most biological materials are diamagnetic, such as proteins, DNA and lipids.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge stated in the introduction.

claim: SMFs can align large biological objects that have diamagnetic anisotropy, such as microtubule polymers and nucleic acid chains.
source: SMFs can align large biological objects that have diamagnetic anisotropy, such as microtubule polymers and nucleic acid chains, as well as some types of cells and organisms (Maret and Dransfeld, 1977; Torbet and Ronzière, 1984; Higashi et al., 1993; Emura et al., 2001; Takeuchi et al., 2002; Teodori et al., 2006; Stern-Straeter et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The degree of alignment with the externally applied magnetic field is proportional to the product of the molecular magnetic susceptibility and the magnetic field strength.
source: The degree of alignment with the externally applied magnetic field is proportional to the product of the molecular magnetic susceptibility and the magnetic field strength.
evidence: This is a theoretical principle stated in the introduction.

claim: For proteins, the diamagnetic anisotropy is mainly due to the alpha helix, beta sheet and aromatic rings.
source: For proteins, the diamagnetic anisotropy is mainly due to the alpha helix, beta sheet and aromatic rings (Chabre, 1978; Worcester, 1978; Pauling, 1979).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Individual peptide bonds have weak diamagnetic anisotropy that can contribute when linked together in a fixed and organized orientation in alpha helix or beta sheet.
source: Even individual peptide bonds, which have weak diamagnetic anisotropy can contribute when linked together in a fixed and organized orientation in alpha helix or beta sheet.
evidence: This is established knowledge about protein structure and magnetic properties.

claim: The DNA chain has relatively large diamagnetic anisotropy mainly due to its stacked aromatic bases.
source: The DNA chain is another example of a biopolymer with relatively large diamagnetic anisotropy (Maret et al., 1975), mainly due to its stacked aromatic bases.
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Theoretical predictions suggested that mitotic chromosome arms might generate electromagnetic fields along the chromosome arm direction.
source: Theoretical predictions suggested that mitotic chromosome arms, where DNA is highly compacted, might generate electromagnetic fields along the chromosome arm direction (Zhao and Zhan, 2012)
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from a cited source.

claim: Chromosomes should be fully aligned by SMFs of around 1.4 T according to theoretical predictions.
source: and, less speculatively, that chromosomes should be fully aligned by SMFs of around 1.4 T (Maret, 1990).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from a cited source.

claim: Purified microtubules can be aligned by moderate and high SMFs and the alignment effect increases significantly with magnetic field strength.
source: Multiple studies have shown that purified microtubules can be aligned by moderate and high SMFs and the alignment effect increases significantly with magnetic field strength (Vassilev et al., 1982; Bras et al., 1998; Glade and Tabony, 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: The alignment of purified microtubules by SMF is due to the diamagnetic anisotropy of tubulin and microtubules.
source: This is due to the diamagnetic anisotropy of tubulin and microtubules (Bras et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Tubulin assembly in vitro was disordered by a 10–100 nT hypogeomagnetic field.
source: In addition, tubulin assembly in vitro was disordered by a 10–100 nT hypogeomagnetic field (natural geomagnetic field is usually around 50000 nT/0.5 Gauss) (Wang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a finding from a cited study.

claim: Whether SMF can change the mitotic spindle orientation in a cell has never been reported prior to this study.
source: However, whether SMF can change the mitotic spindle orientation in a cell has never been reported.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: 16.7 T large gradient SMFs can affect the division orientation of Xenopus eggs.
source: Denegre et al found that 16.7 T large gradient SMFs can affect the division orientation of Xenopus eggs (Denegre et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a finding from a cited study.

claim: Metaphase spindles can orient themselves parallel to the substrate in the absence of aster microtubules in both MDCK and HeLa cells.
source: Although the importance of aster microtubules in spindle orientation determination in some types of cells is well known (Palmer et al., 1992; Shaw et al., 1997), the metaphase spindles still can orient themselves parallel to the substrate in the absence of aster microtubules in both Madin-Darby Canine Kidney (MDCK) and human cervical cancer HeLa cells (Lazaro-Dieguez et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: The microtubule and actin cytoskeleton in interphase cells could be affected by 7–17 T ultra-high SMFs in some cell types.
source: Although a few reports in recent years showed that the microtubule and actin cytoskeleton in interphase cells could be affected by 7–17 T ultra-high SMFs in some cell types (Valiron et al., 2005), information about the mitotic spindle was not provided.
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: Prolonged treatment of 1 T moderate intensity SMF can cause multipolar spindles in cells.
source: In our previous study, we found that prolonged treatment of 1 T moderate intensity SMF can cause multipolar spindles in cells (Luo et al., 2016)
evidence: This is a finding from the authors' previous study.

claim: Stronger SMFs are likely to produce more obvious effects on spindles than 1 T SMF.
source: and we predict that stronger SMFs are likely to produce more obvious effects on spindles.
evidence: This is a prediction based on previous findings.

claim: The WM4 magnet provides vertical ultra-high homogenous SMF at the center of the magnet.
source: The WM4 magnet we use (Figure 1A) provides vertical ultra-high homogenous SMF at the center of the magnet.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental apparatus shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The magnetic field direction in the WM4 magnet is upward.
source: The magnetic field direction is upward.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental setup.

claim: Bright field microscopic observation and flow cytometry did not reveal obvious changes of cell morphology or cell death after 4 hr of 27 T SMF exposure in CNE-2Z cells.
source: Bright field microscopic observation and flow cytometry did not reveal obvious changes of cell morphology or cell death after 4 hr of 27 T SMF exposure in human nasopharyngeal carcinoma CNE-2Z cell (Figure 2A–D; Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 2A-D.

claim: Immunostaining analysis did not reveal obvious microtubule or actin cytoskeleton abnormalities in interphase CNE-2Z cells after 4 hr of 27 T exposure.
source: Moreover, immunostaining analysis did not reveal obvious microtubule or actin cytoskeleton abnormalities in interphase cells after 4 hr of 27 T exposure either (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: 27 T SMF treatment for 4 hr is not acutely toxic to CNE-2Z cells.
source: Therefore 27 T SMF treatment for 4 hr is not acutely toxic to CNE-2Z cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental observations in Figure 2.

claim: Cell morphology was not obviously changed three days post-exposure to 27 T SMF.
source: In addition, we found that the cell morphology was not obviously changed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A) three days post-exposure
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Cell number decreased by ~40% three days post-exposure to 27 T SMF.
source: but the cell number decreased by ~40% (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The cell cycle was only slightly changed three days post-exposure to 27 T SMF.
source: Flow cytometry analysis showed that the cell cycle was only slightly changed (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C)
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Cell death was not obviously affected three days post-exposure to 27 T SMF.
source: while the cell death was not obviously affected (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Mitotic spindle orientation was perturbed by 27 T SMF in CNE-2Z cells.
source: Using immunofluorescence analysis of cells fixed immediately after they were taken out of the magnet, we found that mitotic spindle orientation was perturbed by 27 T SMF (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: In sham incubated or control cells, the mitotic spindle axis is usually parallel to the tissue culture plate or coverslip ('lateral').
source: In sham incubated or control cells, the mitotic spindle axis is usually parallel to the tissue culture plate or coverslip ('lateral')
evidence: This is an observation from the control experiments.

claim: 27 T magnetic field increased the percentage of spindles that were not parallel to the coverslip ('non-lateral').
source: while the 27 T magnetic field increased the percentage of spindles that were not parallel to the coverslip ('non-lateral') (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 3A,B.

claim: Non-lateral metaphase spindles were increased by 27 T SMF.
source: We separately measured metaphase spindles (Figure 3C; Figure 3—source data 1) as well as prometaphase and metaphase spindles together (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and both results showed that non-lateral spindles were increased by 27 T SMF.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: 4 hr of exposure to 0.05 T and 1 T SMFs does not increase the non-lateral spindles as 27 T SMF does.
source: We found that 4 hr of exposure does not increase the non-lateral spindles (Figure 4B; Figure 4—source data 1) as 27 T SMF.
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: 4 hr of 9 T exposure does not increase the non-lateral spindles.
source: We also tested 9 T SMF provided by a superconducting magnet (Zhang et al., 2016) and found that 4 hr of 9 T exposure does not increase the non-lateral spindles either (Figure 4C; Figure 4—source data 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Exposure for a prolonged time of 3 days to 0.05 T or 1 T SMFs had no effect on spindle orientation.
source: However, although exposure for a prolonged time of 3 days to 0.05 T or 1 T SMFs still had no effect (Figure 4D; Figure 4—source data 3)
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: 9 T SMF treatment for 3 days could perturb spindle orientation.
source: 9 T SMF treatment for 3 days could perturb spindle orientation (Figure 4E; Figure 4—source data 4).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: 0.05 T and 1 T SMFs had no effect on spindle orientation even after 7 days of exposure.
source: In contrast, 0.05 T and 1 T SMFs had no effect on spindle orientation even after 7 days of exposure (Figure 4F; Figure 4—source data 5).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The effect of SMF on spindle orientation is field intensity-dependent and time-dependent.
source: Therefore the effect of SMF on spindle orientation was field intensity-dependent and time-dependent.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings shown in Figures 3-4.

claim: Ultra-high SMF of 27 T could change spindle orientation in 4 hr but 9 T SMF need 3 days to show effects.
source: Ultra-high SMF of 27 T could change spindle orientation in 4 hr but 9 T SMF need 3 days to show effects.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings shown in Figures 3-4.

claim: In the 27 T SMF treated group, prometaphase cells tended to orient with their spindle long axis in parallel with the field direction.
source: Interestingly, spindle orientation was different in prometaphase cells vs. metaphase cells (Figure 5E). In the 27 T SMF treated group, prometaphase cells tended to orient with their spindle long axis in parallel with the field direction
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: In the 27 T SMF treated group, metaphase cells tended to orient with the spindle long axis normal to the field direction.
source: while metaphase cells tended to orient with the spindle long axis normal to the field direction (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: 27 T SMF had similar orientation effects on CNE-2Z and RPE1 spindles.
source: As shown in Figure 5F (Figure 5—source data 1) and Figure 5G (Figure 5—source data 2), 27 T SMF had similar orientation effects on CNE-2Z and RPE1 spindles.
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 5F and 5G.

claim: The main difference between cells in prometaphase and metaphase is the organization of chromosomes, which are distributed in prometaphase and tightly aligned in metaphase.
source: The main difference between cells in prometaphase and metaphase is the organization of chromosomes, which are distributed in prometaphase and tightly aligned in metaphase.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about cell cycle stages.

claim: The difference in chromosome organization between prometaphase and metaphase accounts for the differential response to magnetic fields.
source: We suspect this difference accounts for the differential response to magnetic fields.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The chromosome distribution in spindles affects the angle between spindle long axis and the magnetic field/gravity direction.
source: After quantifying four independent coverslips for both CNE-2Z and RPE1 cells, we found that the chromosome distribution in spindles seemed to affect the angle between spindle long axis and the magnetic field/gravity direction (Figure 6D, Figure 6—source data 1 and Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The preferred spindle orientation relative to the field differs significantly between cells that have well aligned chromosomes and misaligned chromosomes.
source: The preferred spindle orientation relative to the field differed between cells that have well aligned chromosomes and misaligned chromosomes, and that this difference was significant (p<0.01 in RPE1 cells and p<0.05 in CNE-2Z cells) (Figure 6E, Figure 6—source data 2, Figure 6F, Figure 6—source data 3).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 6E and 6F with statistical significance.

claim: Chromosomes play a major role in spindle orientation in response to SMFs.
source: This indicates that chromosomes play a major role in spindle orientation in response to SMFs.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings with CENP-E inhibitor.

claim: Spindles with misaligned chromosomes tend to align with the spindle long axis in parallel with the field direction.
source: Spindles with misaligned chromosomes tend to align with the spindle long axis in parallel with the field direction
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the CENP-E inhibitor experiments.

claim: Spindles with well aligned chromosomes tend to align their metaphase plate in parallel with the field direction.
source: while spindles with well aligned chromosomes tend to align their metaphase plate in parallel with the field direction (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from the CENP-E inhibitor experiments shown in Figure 6G.

claim: Lower magnetic fields of 1 T or 9 T treatment for 4 hr did not affect the spindle orientation in CENP-E inhibitor treated cells.
source: Not surprisingly, lower magnetic fields of 1 T or 9 T treatment for 4 hr did not affect the spindle orientation (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Spindles aligned normal to the magnetic field direction were wider than those parallel to the field direction.
source: We also noted that spindles aligned normal to the magnetic field direction were wider than those parallel to the field direction (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is an experimental observation supported by data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: In 27 T SMF-treated cells, spindles normal to the field direction have bigger spindle pole angles, which makes them look 'wider', compared to the ones parallel to the field direction.
source: In both synchronized and unsynchronized CNE-2Z and RPE1 cells, the spindles in 27 T SMF-treated cells that were normal to the field direction has bigger spindle pole angles, which makes them look 'wider' (Figure 7C, Figure 7—source data 1 and Figure 7—figure supplement 1) compare to the ones parallel to the field direction.
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: In control cells not treated with SMFs, the spindle pole angles are similar in both directions.
source: In control cells that were not treated with SMFs, the spindle pole angles are similar in both directions (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is an experimental finding from control experiments shown in Figure 7C.

claim: The spindle length was not much affected by the 27 T magnetic field.
source: To get a more quantitative measurement, we quantified the spindle length (a) and width (w) and found that the spindle length was not much affected by the 27 T magnetic field (Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,B)
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,B.

claim: The spindle width was increased in both CNE-2Z and RPE1 cells when the spindle was normal to the field direction.
source: but the spindle width was increased in both CNE-2Z and RPE1 cells, when the spindle was normal to the field direction (Figure 7D, Figure 7—source data 2 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2C,D)
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Chromosome alignment or misalignment affects the spindle ellipticity in the presence of 27 T field.
source: It is interesting that the chromosome alignment or misalignment did actually affect the spindle ellipticity (Figure 7F, Figure 7—source data 3).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Spindles with well aligned chromosomes became obviously wider in 27 T (p<0.005).
source: Our results show that spindles with well aligned chromosomes became obviously wider in 27 T (p<0.005)
evidence: This is an experimental finding with statistical significance.

claim: The morphology of spindles with misaligned chromosomes was not much affected by 27 T SMF.
source: but the morphology of spindles with misaligned chromosomes was not much affected (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is an experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Spindles with well aligned chromosomes are slightly wider in the sham control group compared to spindles with misaligned chromosomes.
source: We also noticed that spindles with well aligned chromosomes themselves are slightly wider in the sham control group compared to spindles with misaligned chromosomes (Figure 7F)
evidence: This is an experimental observation from control experiments shown in Figure 7F.

claim: The SMF-induced spindle orientation and morphology changes are due to the combined alignment effects of both microtubules and chromosomes in the magnetic field.
source: We propose that the SMF-induced spindle orientation and morphology changes are due to the combined alignment effects of both microtubules and chromosomes in the magnetic field (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental findings.

claim: When the field is oriented normal to the substrate, magnetic torques on both microtubules and chromatin may combine to re-orient spindles away from the surface plane, opposing torques on astral microtubules that promote the normal orientation.
source: When the field is oriented normal to the substrate, magnetic torques on both microtubules and chromatin may combine to re-orient spindles away from the surface plane, opposing torques on astral microtubules that promote the normal orientation.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental findings.

claim: Application of the magnetic field parallel to the coverslip allowed discrimination of torques on chromatin vs. microtubules.
source: Application of the magnetic field parallel to the coverslip allowed us to discriminate torques on chromatin vs. microtubules
evidence: This is a description of the experimental approach.

claim: Torques on well aligned chromatin dominated, aligning spindles preferentially with their microtubules normal to the field, and their metaphase plate parallel to the field.
source: and in this case it appears that torques on well aligned chromatin dominated, aligning spindles preferentially with their microtubules normal to the field, and their metaphase plate parallel to the field (Figures 5 and 6).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings shown in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: The result is opposite to that proposed by Denegre et al, who studied Xenopus egg cleavage in 16.7 T high magnetic fields.
source: Our result is opposite to that proposed by Denegre et al, who studied Xenopus egg cleavage in 16.7 T high magnetic fields and theoretically proposed that the orientation of spindle in magnetic field is a result of the balance between aster microtubules and spindle microtubules (Denegre et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work from a cited study.

claim: The cleavage plane in Xenopus eggs is oriented by huge microtubule asters with almost mm dimensions, while the amount of chromatin is the same as a mitotic cell.
source: The cleavage plane in Xenopus eggs is oriented by huge microtubule asters with almost mm dimensions, while the amount of chromatin is the same as a mitotic cell.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about Xenopus eggs.

claim: The ratio of chromatin to microtubules is much larger in human somatic cells compared to Xenopus eggs.
source: In contrast, the ratio of chromatin to microtubules is much larger in human somatic cells.
evidence: This is a comparison based on biological knowledge.

claim: Theoretical calculation predicted that the highly compacted mitotic chromosomes could be fully aligned by magnetic fields at around 1.4 T.
source: Theoretical calculation predicted that the highly compacted mitotic chromosomes could be fully aligned by magnetic fields at around 1.4 T (Maret, 1990).
evidence: This is a theoretical prediction from a cited source.

claim: The metaphase plate composed of chromosomes likely dominated the SMF-induced orientation in normal-sized somatic cells.
source: Therefore the metaphase plate composed of chromosomes likely dominated the SMF-induced orientation in normal-sized somatic cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on theoretical predictions and experimental findings.

claim: The torque of a substance is equal to the product of magnetic field intensity and the magnetic susceptibility of the object.
source: The torque of a substance is equal to the product of magnetic field intensity and the magnetic susceptibility of the object, in which the susceptibility could also be field-dependent and can be Taylor expanded.
evidence: This is a physical principle.

claim: The torque could be parabolically proportional to the magnetic field strength.
source: This means that the torque could be parabolically proportional to the magnetic field strength.
evidence: This is a theoretical inference from physical principles.

claim: A high field has much more severe impact than a low field as far as field-induced alignment is concerned, and the relationship is not linear.
source: Thus, a high field has much more severe impact than a low field as far as field-induced alignment is concerned, and the relationship is not linear.
evidence: This is a theoretical inference from physical principles.

claim: 10 T or 13 T SMFs did not have obvious effects on human-hamster hybrid (AL) cells, Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells or human primary skin fibroblasts (AG1522) cells.
source: Nakahara et al and Zhao et al showed that 10 T or 13 T SMFs did not have obvious effects on the human-hamster hybrid (AL) cells, Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells or human primary skin fibroblasts (AG1522) cells (Nakahara et al., 2002; Zhao et al., 2010)
evidence: This is a finding from cited studies.

claim: 12-16-12T large gradient SMFs can affect microtubule actin crosslinking factor 1 (MACF1) expression and its association with cytoskeleton.
source: the Shang group found that 12-16-12T large gradient SMFs can affect microtubule actin crosslinking factor 1 (MACF1) expression and its association with cytoskeleton (Qian et al., 2009)
evidence: This is a finding from a cited study.

claim: 12-16-12T large gradient SMFs can affect osteoblast ultrastructure and cell viability by disrupting collagen I or Febronectin/αβ1 integrin in human osteoblast-like cell lines.
source: as well as osteoblast ultrastructure and cell viability by disrupting collagen I or Febronectin/αβ1 integrin in human osteoblast-like cell lines (Qian et al., 2013)
evidence: This is a finding from a cited study.

claim: Valiron et al did not observe strong cell killing effects with 17 T SMF.
source: Valiron et al used 17 T, the highest SMF strength applied on cells so far and they did not observe strong cell killing effects (Valiron et al., 2005).
evidence: This is a finding from a cited study.

claim: The cytoskeleton of interphase mouse embryo fibroblast 3T3 cells and human cervical cancer HeLa cells can be affected by 17 T SMF.
source: Instead, they found that the cytoskeleton of interphase mouse embryo fibroblast 3T3 cells and human cervical cancer HeLa cells can be affected by 17 T SMF.
evidence: This is a finding from a cited study.

claim: 27 T SMF does not have an immediate cell killing effects on human CNE-2Z and RPE1 cells but it changes the mitotic spindle orientation and morphology.
source: Here we found that 27 T SMF does not have an immediate cell killing effects on human CNE-2Z and RPE1 cells but it changes the mitotic spindle orientation and morphology.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: The spindle orientation change induced by ultra-high SMF is likely conserved between different cell types, although there may be variations among them.
source: The spindle orientation change induced by ultra-high SMF is likely conserved between different cell types, although there may be variations among them.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on observations in CNE-2Z and RPE1 cells.

claim: Mitotic chromosomes have electromagnetic properties.
source: However, it has been shown that the mitotic chromosomes have electromagnetic properties (Zhao and Zhan, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge from a cited study.

claim: The direction of mitotic spindle alignment in the magnetic field depends on how the diamagnetic anisotropies of its individual components, including microtubules and chromosomes, align within it.
source: Based on theoretical calculation and experimental validation, Valles and his colleagues proposed that the direction of mitotic spindle alignment in the magnetic field depends on how the diamagnetic anisotropies of its individual components, including microtubules and chromosomes, align within it (Valles, 2002; Valles et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a theoretical proposal from cited studies.

claim: In Xenopus eggs, the cleavage plane, which is perpendicular to the spindle long axis, tends to parallel with the magnetic field direction.
source: Denegre et al's results about Xenopus egg division shows that the cleavage plane, which is perpendicular to the spindle long axis, tend to parallel with the magnetic field direction (Denegre et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a finding from a cited study.

claim: Xenopus eggs have very different long astral microtubules, which composed a large portion of the whole cell.
source: Xenopus eggs have very different long astral microtubules, which composed a large portion of the whole cell.
evidence: This is established biological knowledge about Xenopus eggs.

claim: Most human somatic cells have much less astral microtubules and much bigger spindle microtubules compared to Xenopus eggs.
source: In contrast, the cells used in our study as well as most human somatic cells have much less astral microtubules and much bigger spindle microtubules compared to Xenopus eggs.
evidence: This is a comparison based on biological knowledge.

claim: The relative contribution of astral and spindle microtubules, as well as chromosomes, will be critical to determine the final outcome of magnetic field effects in a given cell type.
source: Since both astral and spindle microtubules, as well as chromosomes respond to magnetic field, their relative contribution will be critical to determine the final outcome in a given cell type.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental findings and comparisons with other systems.

claim: Ultra-high magnetic field can change the orientation and morphology of mitotic spindles.
source: Our study not only found that ultra-high magnetic field can change the orientation and morphology of mitotic spindles, but also provided a tool to probe the role of spindle orientation and perturbation in developmental and cancer biology.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: This study provides a tool to probe the role of spindle orientation and perturbation in developmental and cancer biology.
source: Our study not only found that ultra-high magnetic field can change the orientation and morphology of mitotic spindles, but also provided a tool to probe the role of spindle orientation and perturbation in developmental and cancer biology.
evidence: This is a proposed application of the findings.
